title: Prime Video Takes Global on Turkish AI-Generated Movie 'Çukur:Vartolu'
source_used: Variety (read from the pre-fetched full text)
key_facts: Prime Video has taken global rights to 'Çukur: Vartolu', an AI movie from Turkish producer Ay Yapim, spun off from its hit series 'Çukur' (known internationally as 'The Pit').

The film is produced by Ay Yapim's Singapore-based AI studio, AI Yapim, which in August launched the AI-generated historical drama 'Castle Walls' on Prime Video; that show had two 15-minute episodes and was touted as the first show made end-to-end with AI to appear on a major global streamer.
AI Yapim says it is taking its AI-native production approach 'from an original story to an established drama franchise'.
Ay Yapim says 'Çukur' has aired on free-to-air television in 105 countries since its 2017 premiere and that the show's official YouTube channel has passed 6.4 billion cumulative views.
The film opens a new chapter in the series' world, built around the childhood and origins of Vartolu Sadettin, the illegitimate son of the Koçovalı family.

Ay Yapim says every frame was generated with AI, from the characters' faces to every setting, but the acting is human: actors performed the scenes and AI generated the characters over their movement, timing and expression, and all dialogue was recorded by human voice actors.
Variety adds that it will be interesting to see how viewers of the live-action 'Çukur' react to the AI-generated spin-off.
The article gives no release date.
quote_evidence: "Every frame of the film was generated with AI, from the characters' faces to every setting," the Ay Yapim statement said.
"The acting is human: actors performed the scenes, and AI generated the characters over their movement, timing and expression. All dialogue was recorded by human voice actors."
Prime Video has taken global rights to Turkish TV powerhouse Ay Yapim's AI movie "Çukur: Vartolu," a spin-off from its hit series "Çukur," known internationally as "The Pit."
why_it_matters_hint: A major streamer is carrying an AI-visual film built on an established franchise, a test of audience and industry acceptance, though the AI claims come from the producer's statement.
notes: Variety's report rests on a statement from Ay Yapim; Prime Video is not quoted. The AI-production claims, the 105 countries and the 6.4 billion views are the producer's own. 'Amazon's Prime Video' uses general knowledge (not in the article).
